latin.553: §. XIII. Etsi verò ab hoc, ad Reformationis usque tempora perversissima, Nicænorum tam de incorruptibilis Dei in Imaginem hominis corruptibilis, quàm de panis Eucharistici in Corporis Christi Substantiam Transmutatione agraphô quin antigraphô, Sententia primas tenuerit, longe lateque disseminanda; inventi tamen etiam SECULO NONO, hinc inde sunt, qui utrique Transsubstantiationi pro virili reclamarent. Enimverò circa ipsum Seculi Noni ingressum, divus Imperator CAROLUS, jure suô MAGNUS appellatus, sicuti imaginum venerationem usumque sacrum, per Francofurtense Concilium, intra certos saltem limites, coërcuit Anno 794.; ita de Eucharistia quoque sanorum Christi verborum formam, in Epistola sua ad Alcuinum, luculenter satis hisce expressit: Cœnando, inquit, cum Discipulis Christus, panem fregit & calicem pariter dedit iis in FIGURAM corporis & sanguinis sui, nobisque profuturum magnum exhibuit Sacramentum.
latin.554: Procedente Seculô & ad medium sui assurgente, Caroli M. Nepos, initiô Rex Franciæ, mox Imperator quoque sat inclitus, CAROLUS CALVUS, veritatis Evangelicæ, etiam in doctrina de Eucharistia percupidus, tum Bertramo Presbytero, tùm Erigena Scoto, de corpore & sanguine Domini Tractatus scribere jussit, ex quorum priori, cum adhuc in manibus eruditorum versetur, quasdam propositiones veritatem Eucharisticam illustraturas, hic adduxisse operæ pretium ducimus.
latin.555: Ac (1) quidem, verborum Institutionis Christi improprietatem edocturus Bertramus: Panis vinumque, ait ille, FIGURATE Christi corpus & sanguis existunt. Itemque: Iste panis & calix, qui corpus & sanguis Christi nominantur, memoriam representant Dominicæ Passionis sive mortis, quemadmodum ipse in Evangelio dixit: Hoc facite in meam commemorationem. Quod exponens Apostolus Paulus ait: quotiescunque manducaveritis panem & calicem biberitis, mortem Domini annunciabitis, donec veniat. Docemur à Salvatore nec non à S. Paulo Apostolo, quod iste panis & iste sanguis, qui super altare ponuntur, in FIGURAM sive memoriam Dominicæ mortis ponuntur, ut quod gestum est in præterito, præsenti revocet memoria, ut illius passionis memores effecti, per eam efficiamur divini muneris consortes, per quam sumus à morte liberati.
latin.556: (II) Naturale corpus Christi, modô corporali, in Cena non præsens esse, inculcaturus, significantissimè ita scribit: Corpus & Sanguis quod in Ecclesia geritur (i. e. quod manibus Ministrorum in Ecclesia tractatur, manibusque & ore accipitur) differt ab illo corpore & sanguine quod in Christi corpore per resurrectionem jam glorificatum cognoscitur: Et hoc Corpus (nempe Eucharisticus panis) SIGNUM est & SPECIES; illud verò ipsa veritas. Hoc enim geritur, donec ad illud perveniatur. Ubi verò ad illud perventum fuerit, hoc removebitur. Apparet ita quod multâ inter se differentia separantur, quantum est inter pignus & eam rem pro qua pignus traditur, & quantum inter imaginem & rem cujus est imago, & quantum inter speciem & veritatem. Hic nemo arbitretur contendere Bertramum, umbram, & non veritatem in sacramento sumi (perpetuò enim, ut paulò post dicemus, cibo Spirituali potuque Fidelium animas in S. Cœna pasci allaborat inculcare); Sed quod negat hic Bertramus, istud solum est: Verum & naturale corpus Christi Ore corporis manducari.
latin.557: (III) Nec naturale corpus Christi, Corporaliter, seu Oraliter, in Cœna manducari evicturus, quæstionem hanc ex professo proponit: Utrum ipsum corpus quod de Maria natum & passum, mortuum & sepultum, quodque ad Dextram Patris residet, sit, quod ore Fidelium per Sacramentorum mysterium, in Ecclesia quotidie sumatur? Et respondet ex Ambrosio per Scripturam loquente… Non secundum hoc, quod videtur, quod corporaliter sumitur, quod dente premitur, quod fauce glutitur… æterna vita substantiam subministrat… Interim tamen (IV.) Spiritualem corporis Christi tàm præsentiam quam participationem pleno ore confessurus, in Responsione ad priorem Imperatoris quæstionem: Num Mysteriôso quôdam modô corpus Christi in Cœna à Fidelibus sumatur? occupatus, inter alia ita respondet: Quandoquidem omnium confessione corpus & sanguis Christi in Cœna sumitur, necesse est, panem & vinum in melius quoddam transiisse, mutationemque hanc non CORPORALITER, sed SPIRITUALITER contigisse, ut jam nunc rectè dicatur, mutationem dictam FIGURATIVE factam esse, subque tegumento corporalis panis & vini, SPIRITUALE CORPUS ET SPIRITUALEM SANGUINEM Christi, actu præsentem esse… Quoniam est SPIRITUALIS ESCA, est SPIRITUALIS POTUS, spiritualiter pascens & æternæ satietatis vitam tribuens.
latin.558: Adhuc disertius Johannem Scotum Erigenam, omnem Bertrami, Coævi sui & Comilitionis, à Carolo Calvo unà evocati, de Eucharistia traditam veritatem enunciasse scriptoque comprehendisse, etsi ejus Tractatus injuria temporum deperditus, vel potiùs Pontificis Romani & aliorum malevolorum perverso zelô, traditus Vulcano sit, fidem faciunt alia Viri hujus Scripta, de Divisione naturæ, per Oxonienses, Anno superioris seculi 81. ab interitu vindicata… Aliorum Seculi Noni Scriptorum de Eucharistia Orthodoxorum testimonia, Amalarii puta, Rabani Mauri, Walafridi Strabonis, ut & ipsius Bertrami, contra Pontificios vindicata vide apud Dunelmensem à p. 88. ad p. 97.

pass_a.553: §. XIII. Although indeed from this point all the way to the most perverse times of the Reformation the Nicaeans’ Sentence — both concerning the Transmutation of the incorruptible God into the Image of corruptible man and concerning that of the Eucharistic bread into the Substance of Christ’s Body, unwritten and even anti-written — held first place, to be disseminated far and wide; yet even in the NINTH AGE there were found here and there who for their part would cry out against both Transubstantiations. For around the very entrance of the Ninth Age, the divine Emperor CHARLES, rightly called the GREAT, just as he restrained the veneration and sacred use of images by the Frankfurt Council within certain limits at least in the year 794, so also concerning the Eucharist he expressed the form of Christ’s sound words clearly enough in his Letter to Alcuin in these words: Dining, he says, with the Disciples, Christ broke bread and likewise gave them the cup in the FIGURE of His body and blood, and exhibited to us a great Sacrament that would profit us.
pass_a.554: As the Age proceeded and rose toward its middle, Charles the Great’s Grandson, at first King of France, soon also a sufficiently illustrious Emperor, CHARLES THE BALD, most eager for Evangelical truth even in the doctrine of the Eucharist, ordered both Bertram the Presbyter and Erigena the Scot to write Treatises on the body and blood of the Lord — from the former of which, since it is still turned in the hands of the learned, we judge it worth the labor to have brought here certain propositions that will illustrate the Eucharistic truth.
pass_a.555: And (1) indeed, Bertram about to teach the impropriety of Christ’s Institution words: Bread and wine, he says, exist FIGURATIVELY as Christ’s body and blood. Likewise: This bread and cup, which are named the body and blood of Christ, represent the memory of the Lord’s Passion or death, just as He Himself said in the Gospel: Do this in remembrance of me. Which the Apostle Paul explaining says: as often as you shall have eaten the bread and drunk the cup, you will announce the Lord’s death until He come. We are taught by the Savior and also by S. Paul the Apostle that this bread and this blood, which are set upon the altar, are set in the FIGURE or memory of the Lord’s death, so that what was done in the past may recall present memory, that made mindful of His passion we may through it be made partakers of the divine gift through which we have been freed from death.
pass_a.556: (II) About to inculcate that Christ’s natural body is not present in the Supper in a corporal mode, he writes most significantly thus: The Body and Blood which is handled in the Church (i.e. which is treated by the Ministers’ hands in the Church and received by hands and mouth) differs from that body and blood which is known in Christ’s body already glorified through the resurrection: And this Body (namely the Eucharistic bread) is a SIGN and SPECIES; but that is the truth itself. For this is handled until one arrives at that. But when one shall have arrived at that, this will be removed. So it appears they are separated by much difference among themselves — as much as between a pledge and the thing for which the pledge is handed over, and between an image and the thing of which it is the image, and between species and truth. Here let no one think Bertram contends that a shadow and not the truth is taken in the sacrament (for perpetually, as we shall say a little later, he labors to inculcate that the souls of the Faithful are fed in the Sacred Supper with Spiritual food and drink); But what Bertram denies here is this alone: that the true and natural body of Christ is eaten with the Mouth of the body.
pass_a.557: (III) And about to prove that Christ’s natural body is not eaten Corporally or Orally in the Supper, he proposes this question expressly: Whether the very body born of Mary and that suffered, died and was buried, and that sits at the Father’s Right Hand, is what is taken daily by the Faithful’s mouth through the mystery of the Sacraments in the Church? And he answers from Ambrose speaking through Scripture… Not according to this which is seen, which is taken corporally, which is pressed by the tooth, which is swallowed by the throat… does it supply the substance of eternal life… Meanwhile yet (IV.) about to confess with full mouth both the Spiritual presence and the participation of Christ’s body, occupied in the Response to the Emperor’s prior question — Whether in some Mysterious mode Christ’s body is taken by the Faithful in the Supper? — he answers among other things thus: Since by all’s confession the body and blood of Christ are taken in the Supper, it is necessary that bread and wine have passed into something better, and that this mutation has happened not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY, so that now it is rightly said the said mutation was made FIGURATIVELY, and under the covering of corporal bread and wine the SPIRITUAL BODY AND SPIRITUAL BLOOD of Christ are actually present… Because it is SPIRITUAL FOOD, it is SPIRITUAL DRINK, feeding spiritually and granting the life of eternal satiety.
pass_a.558: Still more expressly, that John Scotus Erigena enunciated and comprehended in writing all the Eucharistic truth handed down by Bertram, his Coeval and Fellow-soldier, summoned together by Charles the Bald — although his Treatise by injury of the times is lost, or rather by the perverse zeal of the Roman Pontiff and other malevolents was handed to Vulcan — other Writings of this Man make faith, On the Division of nature, vindicated from destruction by the Oxford men in the year 81 of the prior age… See the testimonies of other Orthodox Writers of the Ninth Age concerning the Eucharist — Amalarius, Rabanus Maurus, Walafrid Strabo, and Bertram himself — vindicated against the Pontificals in Durham from p. 88 to p. 97.

553: §.XIII: though Nicaean sentences on image-transmutation and bread-into-Body held first place until the Reformation, the NINTH age still found reclaimers against both Transubstantiations.

Around its entrance CHARLES THE GREAT restrained image-veneration (Frankfurt 794) and, to Alcuin, said Christ gave bread and cup in the FIGURE of His body and blood — a great Sacrament for our profit.
554: Mid-century: CHARLES THE BALD, eager for Evangelical truth on the Eucharist, ordered Bertram the Presbyter and Erigena the Scot to write treatises on the Lord’s body and blood.
Bertram’s still circulates among the learned — Strimesius draws propositions that illustrate the Eucharistic truth.
555: Bertram (1): Institution words are improper — bread and wine exist FIGURATIVELY as Christ’s body and blood.

Named body and blood, they represent the memory of the Lord’s Passion; set on the altar in the FIGURE or memory of His death, so present memory of what was done may make us partakers of the divine gift.
556: Bertram (II): Christ’s natural body is not present in the Supper in a corporal mode — what ministers handle differs from the glorified body; the Eucharistic bread is SIGN and SPECIES, that is the truth itself (pledge vs thing; image vs reality).
He does not deny truth taken in the sacrament — souls are fed with Spiritual food and drink — he denies only that the true natural body is eaten with the body’s Mouth.
557: Bertram (III): the body born of Mary, dead, risen, at the Father’s right, is not what teeth press and throats swallow daily — that corporal intake does not supply eternal life.

(IV) Yet he confesses Spiritual presence and participation: bread and wine pass into something better not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY — under corporal covering the SPIRITUAL BODY AND BLOOD are actually present; SPIRITUAL FOOD and DRINK.
558: Erigena, Bertram’s coeval fellow summoned by Charles the Bald, stated the same Eucharistic truth — his treatise lost (or burned by hostile zeal), but On the Division of Nature (Oxford recovery) and other writings make faith.
See also Amalarius, Rabanus Maurus, Walafrid Strabo, and Bertram himself vindicated in Durham pp. 88–97. Stop before §.XIV (tenth century).
